dedupe_keys.name: lac megantic runaway train derailment crude oil fires and explosions tsb report r13d0054

description: This case study is the Transportation Safety Board of Canada's railway investigation report R13D0054 into the runaway train derailment and crude oil fires and explosions at Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, on 6 July 2013. Freight train MMA-002, parked unattended on a descending grade at Nantes with 72 tank cars carrying about 7.7 million litres of petroleum crude oil, rolled about 7.2 miles to 65 mph and derailed in the town centre; 63 tank cars and 2 box cars derailed, about 6 million litres spilled, and fires and explosions destroyed 40 buildings, 53 vehicles and the track, killing 47 people and contaminating the downtown area, river and lake. The report gives factual information, analysis, findings on causes and contributing factors, findings as to risk and safety action. It found that securement relied on a locomotive not in proper condition, seven hand brakes were insufficient and untested, a non-standard repair caused the engine fire, and the railway did not give effective training or oversight. Access: the full report is a free web page; no licence is stated. Caveats: a very long narrative report, not a dataset. It suits hazardous cargo, emergency response and oil supply chain risk scenario design, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
